Namespaced dot-key IDs, hand-authored `messages/en.json`. Someone owns key hygiene forever. | | **@neokapi/i18n-react** | **T0** — add and forget | Plain JSX *is* the catalog; a bundler plugin extracts at build time. No `t()` wrappers on JSX text, no message IDs — English source text is the key. | | Lingui | T2 | Source-as-key macros + PO catalogs; lowest marking cost of the classic libraries. | | react-i18next | T2 | The incumbent; biggest ecosystem, same permanent key hygiene. | | react-intl | T3 — avoid here | Maximum per-string boilerplate + hash-ID churn. Only with an existing ICU/TMS mandate. | **My recommendation: next-intl**, unless you specifically want to trade ecosystem-native for near-zero ongoing toil — in which case take neokapi-i18n. That's the one call I'd like from you, because the two paths have genuinely different shapes and you shouldn't convert between key models later. Things that will actually bite you, given your setup: - **next-intl on Next 16 specifically**: Next.js majors have broken its middleware/routing wiring before — the Next 16 `middleware` → `proxy` rename did exactly that. Also a solo maintainer, and message payloads ship to the client unless you scope namespaces per route. Your stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, no i18n yet, and `src/app/page.tsx` is already a Client Component. That's a greenfield decision, so there are two real candidates and the choice is a trade-off, not a lookup. ## The two worth considering | Option | Toil grade | What you're signing up for | |---|---|---| | **next-intl** | **T2** — standing chore | The ecosystem-native App Router choice. Namespaced dot-key IDs, hand-authored `messages/en.json`. Best RSC ergonomics — works in Server Components, no `"use client"` tax. | | **@neokapi/i18n-react** | **T0** — add and forget | Plain JSX *is* the catalog; a webpack-plugin extracts `

Your notes

` at build time. No wrapping, no key hygiene, ever. But the runtime is client-side, so every component rendering translated text needs `"use client"`. | The other libraries don't fit you: **Lingui** (T2) only if the team specifically wants source-as-key with a classic library; **react-i18next** (T2) is the incumbent but has no RSC support, so App Router users end up on next-i18next anyway; **next-i18next** (T2) is for existing i18next investments you don't have; **react-intl** is T3 — maximum boilerplate plus hash-ID churn on every copy edit, only right under an ICU/TMS mandate. ## My recommendation **Go with @neokapi/i18n-react**, because of a detail specific to your app: `page.tsx` is *already* `"use client"`. The main cost of the T0 path — pushing components to the client boundary — is one you've mostly already paid. In exchange you get: leave the JSX exactly as written, and the only marking work is the handful of strings the extractor can't see (`alert("New note")`, and the `notes` array titles/excerpts if those are ever real UI copy rather than user data — which they look like they'd become). A lint pass finds those for you rather than you eyeballing them. **Choose next-intl instead if** you expect this app to lean into Server Components as it grows — data-heavy pages you'd rather render on the server. Then next-intl's server-side `getTranslations` is worth the standing key-hygiene chore, and you avoid making the tree client-rendered to get translated text. One Next 16 caveat either way: next-intl's middleware/routing wiring has historically broken on Next majors — the middleware→proxy rename in 16 did exactly that. It's fixed, but that surface is where you'll spend upgrade time. ## What doesn't change Whichever you pick, the translation pipeline runs through kapi and stays the same: extract → `kapi pseudo-translate --target-lang qps` as a readiness gate (this surfaces hardcoded strings you missed — your `alert()` would show up here) → `kapi translate` per locale → verify the app actually *renders* translated. The catalog being full is not the finish line; the rendered UI is. Want me to set up the neokapi-i18n path, or go with next-intl?

Your stack: Next.js 16.2.10, React 19, App Router (`src/app/page.tsx`), no i18n deps yet — greenfield. ## Recommendation: **next-intl** It's the ecosystem-native choice for the App Router and the de-facto standard there. Grade **T2** on the toil index — a standing chore: someone owns key hygiene and catalog sync, and i18n shows up in sprint planning. - **Idiom:** namespaced dot-key IDs, hand-authored `messages/en.json`. Keep the IDs — don't convert it to source-as-key; its own extraction (`useExtracted`) is still experimental. - **Config that actually earns the T2:** shallow feature-scoped namespaces, pass only the namespaces a tree needs to `NextIntlClientProvider` (otherwise the whole message payload ships to the client), and [lingualdev/i18n-check](https://github.com/lingualdev/i18n-check) in CI — without it, missing keys surface at runtime as rendered key paths. - **Footguns:** Next.js majors have broken its middleware/routing wiring before (Next 16's middleware→proxy rename did exactly that), and it's a solo-maintainer project. Latest verified: 4.13. ## The alternative worth knowing about: **@neokapi/i18n-react** Grade **T0** — "add and forget." Plain JSX *is* the catalog; a bundler plugin extracts `

Your notes

` at build time, so there's no wrapping and no key hygiene at all. The English source text is the key. It works on Next.js via the `webpack` hook, but the runtime is client-side, so every component rendering translated text needs `"use client"` and the first paint has to be gated on the dictionary load. Your `page.tsx` is already a client component, so that cost is currently near zero — it grows if you later push rendering into Server Components. **Pick next-intl if** you want RSC ergonomics and the mainstream option your team can hire and Google for. **Pick neokapi-i18n if** minimizing per-feature toil matters more than being on the ecosystem-standard path and you're comfortable staying client-rendered. Two other options, for completeness: **Lingui** (T2) if the team specifically wants source-as-key macros with a classic library, and **react-intl** — T3, don't, unless you have an existing FormatJS/ICU mandate and a TMS. ## Either way Whichever you choose, translation routes through `kapi` (v1.2.0-rc29 is on your PATH) so terminology, placeholders and format survive — never hand-edit target catalogs. For next-intl that's the `nextjs` preset: ```bash kapi init --framework nextjs --target-locale fr kapi pseudo-translate messages/en.json --target-lang qps # readiness gate, run this first kapi translate messages/en.json --target-lang fr -o messages/fr.json ``` The pseudo-translate pass is the one most stacks lack — it surfaces the hardcoded strings you'd otherwise ship. In your `page.tsx` that would flag the note titles/excerpts in the `notes` array, the `alert("New note")` string, and the footer line. Want me to set one of these up? Say which and I'll wire it in.

events.text:
**Use `next-intl`.** For a Next 16 / React 19 App Router app starting from scratch, it's the default choice.

Why it fits your setup (`next@^16.2.10`, App Router at `src/app`, TypeScript, no i18n yet):

- **Server Components are the primary API**, not an afterthought. `getTranslations()` in RSC, `useTranslations()` in client components, and messages are passed across the boundary explicitly — so you only ship the namespaces a client component actually needs, not the whole catalog.
- **ICU MessageFormat** out of the box — plurals, gender, nested selects, plus `useFormatter` wrapping `Intl.DateTimeFormat`/`NumberFormat`/`RelativeTimeFormat`. You'll need this quickly: "3 notes" vs "1 note" and relative timestamps are exactly where hand-rolled interpolation breaks in Slavic/Arabic locales.
- **Routing is included**: `[locale]` segment, middleware for negotiation/redirects, and locale-aware `Link`/`redirect`/`useRouter` wrappers. This matters because Next's built-in `i18n` key in `next.config` is **Pages Router only** — it does nothing in App Router, so whatever you pick has to solve routing itself.
- **Type-safe keys** via a declaration-merging augmentation, so a typo in `t('titel')` is a compile error.
- Actively maintained and tracking Next releases closely (16-compatible today).

### When I'd pick something else

| Instead | If |
|---|---|
| **Paraglide JS** (inlang) | Bundle size is a hard constraint. Compiles messages into tree-shakable functions — no runtime catalog, no async loading. Trade-off: its own message syntax rather than full ICU, and a smaller ecosystem. |
| **react-i18next / i18next** | Your team already knows it, or you need its plugin ecosystem (runtime HTTP backends, lazy namespaces, exotic detectors). It works in App Router but you wire up the server-side instance and per-request caching yourself. `next-i18next` specifically is Pages Router — don't reach for it here. |
| **Lingui** | You'd rather not maintain a key namespace at all — macros extract messages from the source text. Good DX, but the macro/build integration is more moving parts. |

I would not pick i18next for a greenfield App Router app: you'd be paying integration tax for flexibility you probably don't need.

### What adoption looks like here

Your `src/app/page.tsx` is currently `"use client"` only because of the `onClick`. The natural shape is to move it to `src/app/[locale]/page.tsx` as a **server** component using `getTranslations()`, and split the "New note" button into a small client leaf. Strings like `"Welcome back, {userName}."` and the footer become `messages/en.json` entries; the notes list gives you a real plural case. Flat-or-nested JSON with ICU is also what Crowdin/Lokalise/Phrase ingest natively, so a TMS drops in later without a format migration.

Want me to wire it up — middleware, `[locale]` layout, `en.json`, and the page converted?
